title: Add a Japanese Task Outcome PR summary derived view
rawUserRequest: Japanese capability is mandatory because most adopter engineers use Japanese. Correct every issue found by the comprehensive Japanese assessment before documentation alignment or release, using a separate complete Work Item lifecycle for each issue.

declaredIntent.summary: Render a sanitized Japanese Task Outcome PR fragment from the same approved facts and field policy as the English fragment.

outOfScope: Changing Task Outcome JSON, its allowlisted PR field set, sanitization policy, evidence selection, or opt-in requirement.
Machine-translating arbitrary Outcome prose, evidence, paths, identifiers, statuses, or user-authored values.
Posting to or editing a provider pull request.
Fixing JA-LIFECYCLE-001 or JA-DOC-001 in this Work Item.
Starting documentation alignment, deprecated-assets cleanup, or release.

sources.reason: JA-PR-001 records that the sanitized Task Outcome PR summary chrome is English-only.
The opt-in renderer owns the allowlisted and sanitized PR fragment but currently has fixed English chrome.
The existing Task Outcome derived-view policy establishes strict locale normalization and unchanged arbitrary facts.
Existing regressions bind opt-in, allowlisting, sanitization, empty states, determinism, and non-mutation.
WI-16 fixes JA-PR-001 after JA-STATUS-001 and before lifecycle and uninstall findings.

riskAssessment.reason: Localized labels must not broaden approved fields, weaken redaction, mutate arbitrary prose, or clear the assessment without executable evidence.

executionDecision.reason: The user explicitly authorized correction of every Japanese assessment finding and continuous execution.

preReviewWarnings: Confirm language changes presentation chrome only and the PR-safe field allowlist remains identical.
Verify synthetic sensitive-value/path/unsupported-claim redaction is byte-equivalent in Japanese and English.
Verify unsupported locale requests fail before writing output and do not silently fall back.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The PR renderer accepts a strict supported language selection and derives Japanese chrome from the same opt-in policy, SAFE_FIELDS, sanitization, and source Outcome as English.
Japanese output localizes the title, field labels, and empty marker while preserving status values and arbitrary approved prose byte-for-byte.
Disabled policy still returns an empty fragment in every language; unsupported locale requests fail non-zero before writing an output file.

Japanese and English render exactly the same requested field set and continue excluding provenance, evidence, forced-stop details, synthetic sensitive-value fixtures, absolute paths, and unsupported quantitative claims.
The Make entrypoint passes an explicit language selection without posting to a provider or editing a PR.
Executable tests cover full allowlisted sections, empty/warning states, redaction, deterministic non-mutation, disabled policy, CLI file output, and unsupported locale.
The Japanese assessor requires explicit language support and named executable safety/parity tests before JA-PR-001 can pass.
The machine JSON and derived Markdown assessment are regenerated; JA-PR-001 passes while JA-LIFECYCLE-001 and JA-DOC-001 remain blocking.
The comprehensive plan records implementation evidence, limitations, remaining serial queue, and any process issue found.
Full local finish/archive, one PR, Hosted CI, merge, ai-close-work-item, branch cleanup, and synchronized clean main complete before JA-LIFECYCLE-001 begins.
guidelines: Keep SAFE_FIELDS, opt-in policy, sanitization, and source Outcome single-sourced across languages.
Localize fixed presentation chrome only; never translate or alter arbitrary approved values.
Reject unsupported locales without silent fallback and before writing output.
Test executable CLI and safety parity rather than accepting Japanese keywords in source.
Clear only JA-PR-001 and retain all unrelated Japanese blockers and non-claims.

intent.problem: Task Outcome can produce a Japanese full derived report, but its explicitly approved PR-safe fragment has fixed English chrome. Japanese reviewers cannot obtain a validated sanitized PR fragment, and JA-PR-001 correctly blocks release.
constraints: Preserve the existing pullRequestSummary enabled policy and exact SAFE_FIELDS allowlist.
Apply the same synthetic sensitive-value, absolute-path, and unsupported-claim sanitization in every language.
Preserve status and arbitrary approved prose byte-for-byte; localize fixed labels only.
Do not call a provider API or mutate Outcome JSON.
Leave lifecycle and uninstall findings active and finish this lifecycle before the next corrective.
intent.rationale: A strict language-aware presentation layer on the existing PR-safe renderer gives Japanese reviewers usable output without duplicating facts, widening disclosure, or performing external PR mutations.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An enabled policy selects every SAFE_FIELDS section and requests Japanese.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Japanese and English expose the same field set; only fixed chrome differs and all arbitrary approved values are byte-identical.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add paired full-field rendering assertions and ordered source-value comparisons.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Outcome content contains synthetic sensitive-value fixtures, absolute local paths, unsupported quantitative claims, and non-allowlisted evidence or forced-stop details.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Japanese output applies the same redaction/exclusion boundary as English and reveals none of the unsafe content.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the same adversarial Outcome through both languages and assert exact disclosure parity.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The PR summary policy is disabled or an enabled section is empty.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Disabled remains empty; enabled empty sections use localized chrome without inventing facts.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Extend disabled and empty/warning-state tests across English and Japanese.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A caller requests an unsupported locale through the CLI with an output path.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The command fails non-zero before creating or overwriting the output.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add CLI fail-before-write regression with a sentinel output.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Japanese keywords exist but language wiring or executable safety tests are removed.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Strengthen the assessor to require CLI language support and named Japanese parity/safety tests.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user authorized every Japanese corrective Work Item and its required Make/process changes; this Work Item limits the Makefile edit to explicit PR renderer language passthrough.
